speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly when your wisdom tooth was extracted and have you noticed any unusual bruising or prolonged bleeding from minor cuts in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of prolonged bleeding after other surgeries or dental procedures, such as tonsillectomy? Has your mother or grandmother ever experienced similar bleeding issues?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the bleeding typically stop on its own after a few hours, or does it tend to restart days later? I also need to know if you have ever experienced bleeding into your joints, such as knees or elbows.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, takes no medications. Social history: The patient is a high school student with no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned your uncle has joint swelling, but have you personally experienced any spontaneous joint bleeding or hemarthrosis? REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile (PT, PTT, Platelet Count)

speaker: Doctor
text: Your PTT is prolonged while your PT and platelet count are normal, which strongly suggests a factor VIII or IX deficiency. To distinguish between Hemophilia A and B, I need to know your specific factor levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX Levels
